Ada AD102; dense tensor peaks at the 2.73 GHz this card holds under a bf16 GEMM - not the 2.52 GHz rated boost clock NVIDIA's sheet figures are computed at. GPU Boost clears the rated clock on a GeForce part so the sheet peak is no speed-of-light bound: measured steady 2730 MHz at 388 W / 50 C under the 450 W cap. The MMA ladder measured on this card at 8192^3: bf16 164.5 TFLOPs (471 FLOP/SM/clk), fp8_e4m3 329.6 (943), int8 580.7 (1662) - the hardware's rates are 512 : 1024 : 2048 FLOP/SM/clk, so int8 is 4x bf16 HERE where every datacenter row has it at 2x. That is the GeForce FP32-accumulate halving: int8 accumulates in int32 and is not halved; fp16/bf16 with FP32 accumulate are. Which makes the fp16/bf16 column the FP32-ACCUMULATE rate - what every kernel measured here runs (cuBLAS and Triton both default to it). The same cuBLAS call accumulating in fp16 measured 238.5 TFLOPs, 133% of this column, on the 1024 FLOP/SM/clk path the sheet's 330.3 names: a row measured on an fp16-accumulating kernel is the one case this column understates and needs its own peak rather than a widened one. no NVLink - PCIe Gen4 x16 -> 32 GB/s/dir intra-node; consumer boxes have no RDMA - typical 100 GbE -> 12.5 GB/s/dir cross-node
